story.see: Compare 19 September with 1 October over eastern Uttar Pradesh and the Nepal border plain. Mapped open water is only about 9 square kilometres on 19 September, then about 170 on 1 October and about 130 on 13 October. The new water sits in river valleys and low ground south and north of Gorakhpur.
story.physics: A Bay of Bengal depression that moved inland from about 21 to 27 September brought heavy rain to Uttar Pradesh and Nepal. On 29 September the Ghaghra and Gandak rivers were reported above the danger mark, and an embankment on the Narayani river broke near Tamkuhi Raj in Kushinagar. Officials named heavy rain and water released from barrages as the causes.
story.lband: Calm water is dark to radar, and in this plain the new patches are dark river-valley and field patches that were not there on 19 September. About 8 in 10 of the new water lies inside the largest extent the JRC long-term water record has ever shown here. The total is small next to the whole frame and the 180 metre preview images miss narrow channels, so read this as the clearest wet ground, not the full flood.
story.people: The floodplain here is farmed and densely settled, and the rivers rise from the same monsoon rain that falls over Nepal. Seeing where water still stood days after the rain, and whether it was still there twelve days later, helps show which low fields stay wet longest.

spots.label: Northern plain near the Nepal border
